from PIL import Image, ImageFilter
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
src='/home/user/Desktop/dog_with_background.png'
out='/home/user/Desktop/dog_transparent.png'
im=Image.open(src).convert('RGBA')
arr=np.array(im)
rgb=arr[:,:,:3].astype(np.float32)
h,w=rgb.shape[:2]
# Estimate smooth background color row-by-row from the clean left side of the image.
left_w=min(520, w//3)
row_bg=np.median(rgb[:, :left_w, :], axis=1)
# Smooth the row estimates to avoid reacting to noise.
for c in range(3):
    row_bg[:,c]=ndi.gaussian_filter1d(row_bg[:,c], sigma=18)
diff=rgb-row_bg[:,None,:]
dist=np.sqrt((diff*diff).sum(axis=2))
# Chroma/brightness cues for the husky. The background is blue-gray and low-detail.
luma=(0.299*rgb[:,:,0]+0.587*rgb[:,:,1]+0.114*rgb[:,:,2])
maxc=rgb.max(axis=2); minc=rgb.min(axis=2)
sat=maxc-minc
warm=(rgb[:,:,0]-rgb[:,:,2] > 18) | ((rgb[:,:,0]-rgb[:,:,1] > 8) & (rgb[:,:,1]-rgb[:,:,2] > 8))
dark=luma < 118
very_dark=luma < 80
texture=np.hypot(ndi.sobel(luma,0), ndi.sobel(luma,1))
# Initial foreground: pixels unlike row background or with dog-like dark/warm/texture cues.
fg = (dist > 42) | (dark & (np.indices((h,w))[1] > 520)) | (warm & (np.indices((h,w))[1] > 500) & (luma < 235)) | ((texture > 45) & (np.indices((h,w))[1] > 560))
# Keep only foreground connected to the main dog body. Seeds are known from image composition.
seed=np.zeros((h,w), bool)
seed[40:930, 620:w] = fg[40:930, 620:w]
lab,n=ndi.label(fg)
counts=np.bincount(lab[seed].ravel()) if n else np.array([])
if len(counts)>1:
    counts[0]=0
    main=counts.argmax()
    fg=lab==main
# Fill small holes inside the dog and smooth mask, but keep edges moderately detailed.
fg=ndi.binary_closing(fg, structure=np.ones((5,5)), iterations=2)
fg=ndi.binary_fill_holes(fg)
fg=ndi.binary_opening(fg, structure=np.ones((2,2)), iterations=1)
# Feather the alpha edge.
alpha=(fg.astype(np.uint8)*255)
alpha_img=Image.fromarray(alpha, 'L').filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.2))
# Restore confident dog details such as whiskers/stray black fur around edge.
alpha=np.array(alpha_img)
conf=(fg | ((dist>55) & (np.indices((h,w))[1]>560) & ((dark)|(warm)|(texture>60))))
alpha=np.maximum(alpha, conf.astype(np.uint8)*235)
# Clear definite background still connected to left/top by low distance.
bg_candidate=dist<34
border=np.zeros((h,w), bool); border[:,0]=True; border[0,:]=True; border[:,-1]=False; border[-1,:]=False
lab,n=ndi.label(bg_candidate)
border_labels=np.unique(lab[border & bg_candidate])
conn_bg=np.isin(lab,border_labels)
alpha[conn_bg]=0
rgba=arr.copy(); rgba[:,:,3]=alpha
Image.fromarray(rgba,'RGBA').save(out)
print(out)
print('alpha nonzero pct', (alpha>0).mean()*100, 'bbox', Image.fromarray(alpha).getbbox())
PY"

from PIL import Image, ImageFilter, ImageDraw
import numpy as np
from scipy import ndimage as ndi
src='/home/user/Desktop/dog_with_background.png'
out='/home/user/Desktop/dog_transparent.png'
im=Image.open(src).convert('RGBA')
arr=np.array(im); rgb=arr[:,:,:3].astype(np.float32); h,w=rgb.shape[:2]
yy,xx=np.indices((h,w))
left_w=min(520,w//3)
row_bg=np.median(rgb[:,:left_w,:],axis=1)
for c in range(3): row_bg[:,c]=ndi.gaussian_filter1d(row_bg[:,c],sigma=18)
diff=rgb-row_bg[:,None,:]
dist=np.sqrt((diff*diff).sum(axis=2))
luma=0.299*rgb[:,:,0]+0.587*rgb[:,:,1]+0.114*rgb[:,:,2]
sat=rgb.max(axis=2)-rgb.min(axis=2)
warm=(rgb[:,:,0]-rgb[:,:,2] > 18) | ((rgb[:,:,0]-rgb[:,:,1] > 8) & (rgb[:,:,1]-rgb[:,:,2] > 8))
dark=luma<118
texture=np.hypot(ndi.sobel(luma,0), ndi.sobel(luma,1))
fg=(dist>44) | (dark & (xx>520)) | (warm & (xx>500) & (luma<235)) | ((texture>50) & (xx>560))
lab,n=ndi.label(fg)
seed=(xx>620)&(yy>20)&(yy<h-10)&fg
counts=np.bincount(lab[seed].ravel()) if n else np.array([])
if len(counts)>1:
    counts[0]=0; fg=lab==counts.argmax()
fg=ndi.binary_closing(fg,structure=np.ones((5,5)),iterations=1)
fg=ndi.binary_fill_holes(fg)
# Remove connected background zones that filling pulled into the dog contour.
bg_like=(dist<50) & (sat<42) & (luma>105) & ~((texture>42)&(xx>560))
lab,n=ndi.label(bg_like)
border=np.zeros((h,w),bool); border[:,0]=True; border[0,:]=True
labels=np.unique(lab[border & bg_like])
conn_bg=np.isin(lab,labels)
fg[conn_bg]=False
# Restore confident dog pixels after cleanup.
fg |= ((dist>62)&(xx>570)&(dark|warm|((texture>65)&(luma<230))))
# Keep connected dog component, preserving only small satellites that are edge hairs near it.
lab,n=ndi.label(fg)
seed=(xx>650)&(yy>20)&fg
counts=np.bincount(lab[seed].ravel()) if n else np.array([])
if len(counts)>1:
    counts[0]=0; main=counts.argmax(); fg=lab==main
fg=ndi.binary_opening(fg,structure=np.ones((2,2)),iterations=1)
alpha=np.array(Image.fromarray((fg*255).astype('uint8'),'L').filter(ImageFilter.GaussianBlur(1.0)))
conf=(fg | ((dist>70)&(xx>560)&(dark|warm|texture>75)))
alpha=np.maximum(alpha, conf.astype(np.uint8)*235)
# Hard-clear obvious background connected to left/top one more time.
bg_candidate=(dist<42)&(sat<50)&~dark
lab,n=ndi.label(bg_candidate); labels=np.unique(lab[border & bg_candidate]); conn_bg=np.isin(lab,labels)
alpha[conn_bg]=0
# Make known cursor overlays transparent if they are in empty/edge space; leave dog fur beneath untouched where mask is solid.
# (The source image contains pointer artifacts over the dog; this only removes isolated bright outline pixels.)
cursor=((xx>850)&(xx<925)&(yy>655)&(yy<725)&(luma>185)&(sat<80)&(texture>45))
alpha[cursor & (alpha<245)] = 0
rgba=arr.copy(); rgba[:,:,3]=alpha
Image.fromarray(rgba,'RGBA').save(out)
# preview
chk=Image.new('RGB',(w,h),'white'); d=ImageDraw.Draw(chk); s=40
for y in range(0,h,s):
 for x in range(0,w,s):
  if ((x//s+y//s)&1)==0: d.rectangle([x,y,x+s-1,y+s-1], fill=(210,210,210))
comp=chk.convert('RGBA'); comp.alpha_composite(Image.fromarray(rgba,'RGBA'))
comp.convert('RGB').save('/home/user/Desktop/dog_transparent_preview.png')
print('saved', out)
print('alpha min/max', alpha.min(), alpha.max(), 'transparent pct', (alpha==0).mean()*100, 'bbox', Image.fromarray(alpha).getbbox())
